problems: Protocol gap: the wire op model in protocol/src/ws/ops.ts cannot express several VFS spec §4.4 bodies, so workarounds are in place. (a) `mkdir -p` goes out as an OpBatch of OpCreates, because OpCreate has no items list. (b) OpChmod has no umask field, so perm.ts toWireMode rewrites clauses without a who part into explicit clauses under the caller's umask; a test shows they evaluate identically. (c) OpCopy has no overwrites or noClobber fields, so the server must redo the same merge. (d) OpWrite has no conflictIno, so conflicted copies use deriveIno(opId, ino).

Protocol id collision: `cp -r` derives new ids as deriveIno(opId, srcIno), so two hard links of one source inode would get the same id. copy.ts gives the second link deriveIno(opId, previousDerivedId), and the server must match this.

Batch limits disagree: protocol BATCH_MAX_OPS is 1000 (the syscall schema), while the VFS spec and the ws OpBatch allow 2000. vfs uses VFS_BATCH_MAX_OPS = 2000. The protocol BatchOp also lacks the `link` op of VFS spec §4.3.

Events: the protocol's EVENT_PAYLOADS (syscall-abi §4.6) are one item per event and have no vfs.link, vfs.utimes, vfs.load or vfs.revert topics. vfs emits the §4.5 item arrays internally, and events.ts toBusEvents projects them to the ABI shapes (tested against the protocol schemas). Topics with no ABI entry are not projected.

Outbox spec conflict: the VFS spec keys the outbox by an autoIncrement `seq`; offline-and-sync §4.8 keys it by [osSessionId, cseq]. Migration 001 keeps `seq` and adds a unique index `by_session_cseq`. Coalescing of pending writes (VFS §3.14.2) is not implemented, because offline-and-sync §3.4 says only session.layout records are coalesced.

Spec conflicts with database.md: (a) its tree checksum uses nameHex/targetHex/octal mode, while digest.ts follows VFS §5.6; (b) it bumps the version on nlink changes, while the planners follow VFS §3.2 (no bump). syscall-abi §3.6 allows `link` only for the owner or root, while perm.ts follows VFS §3.7.2 (owner, or both r and w). The VFS spec was followed in all three cases.

Package boundaries: boundaries.js lets the server import only vfs/path and vfs/perm, but PVFS-16 wants names.ts and digest.ts isomorphic as well. The chmod parser and evaluator therefore live in perm.ts (there is no modeparse.ts), so the server can import them.
